title: The Last Letter Revisited
premise: When the coffin of town founder Adelaide Voss is exhumed for the cathedral's centenary and found empty, archivist Jonah Dravenmoor discovers a letter hidden in the crypt wall bearing her own childhood handwriting—a letter she has no memory of writing. Following the letter's clues through the cathedral's sealed records, she uncovers that Adelaide faked her death to escape a controlling family, and that Jonah herself was smuggled out of the Voss household as an infant and raised under another name. The 'closed case' everyone swears by—the 1975 disappearance of Adelaide's granddaughter—was actually a cover story maintained by the very families who now demand the anniversary dinner go undisturbed. At the dinner, Jonah publicly reveals the truth: Adelaide lived out her days in the coastal cottage Jonah now owns, and the empty coffin was Adelaide's final letter to the granddaughter who became Jonah's mother. The case closes not with a culprit but with a homecoming, as Jonah claims both her name and her belonging.
about_author: Bram Whitlock is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one ever asked to read. They write mysteries about the quiet violence of archives and the people buried inside them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Establishes her ordered life in the cathedral archive, her ritual of alphabetizing the town's secrets, and her uneasy relationship with the locked crypt door. When the centenary committee orders Adelaide Voss's exhumation, Jonah alone objects—and is overruled. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into dread.

chapters.title: An Empty House of Oak
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The exhumation draws the whole town; the coffin lid opens on nothing but folded linen and a brass key. Jonah recognizes the key's wax seal from cathedral records she's never been allowed to touch. That night she finds the crypt lock already turned. Emotional beat: vertigo—her ordered world cracking open.

chapters.title: A Letter in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inside the crypt wall she finds a letter dated 1975, written in handwriting identical to her own, addressed to 'the girl who keeps the files.' Forensic document examiner Mara Quist confirms it's genuine—and eerily matches samples of Jonah's writing. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy with a stranger's voice.

chapters.title: The Families Who Signed Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah and councilman Aldous Venn, whose family co-signed a 1975 nondisclosure pact now stored in the restricted vault. Aldous pressures the bishop to halt the investigation before the anniversary dinner. Jonah realizes the 'closed case' has active guardians. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: What the Register Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Digging into baptismal registers, she finds a page razored out in 1976—and a marginal note in Adelaide's hand referencing a 'borrowed daughter.' She confronts her adoptive mother's old friend, who lets slip that Jonah arrived in town as an infant with no paperwork at all. Emotional beat: grief for a self she never knew.

chapters.title: The Cottage by the Grey Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The brass key opens a sea chest in the coastal cottage Jonah inherited years ago—inside, photographs of Adelaide alive decades after her 'death,' and a second letter naming Jonah's birth mother: Adelaide's granddaughter, the missing girl of 1975. Emotional beat: revelation as inheritance.

chapters.title: Threats in Fine Print
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV darkens into menace: he offers Jonah money, then implies her position—and her safety—depend on silence. Meanwhile Mara discovers the exhumation order itself was forged, meaning someone wanted the coffin opened. Emotional beat: the antagonist's mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Toast
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Someone ransacks the archive; the 1975 file burns in the incinerator, but Jonah has already photographed everything. She pieces together the full truth: Adelaide staged her death to flee the family, raised her granddaughter in secret, and arranged for Jonah to inherit the archive itself. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Climax. Multiple POVs converge at the dinner where Aldous plans to declare the matter closed. Jonah stands, projects the photographs and the letters, and reads Adelaide's final words aloud: the empty coffin was a message meant only for her. Aldous's forged exhumation order exposes his family's guilt in the original cover-up. Emotional beat: truth spoken in the lion's den.

chapters.title: Filed Under Home
chapters.summary: Resolution. Jonah's POV. Weeks later, she reopens the crypt as a memorial to Adelaide's real life, files the true record under a new name—her own—and visits the cottage where her mother's letters wait unanswered but read. She belongs to the town now on her own terms. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
